content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1 (₹624) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best policy-compliant plan, but it only lifts the 12:45–14:45 service level to 55.1% against an 80% target.","why":"Calls on general are running long because of the CRM search slowness (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, searches taking 20–40 s). Handle time reached 646.0 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast, while volume and staffing are close to plan. With no action, the 12:45–14:45 window is predicted at 49.7%, with payments at 38.8% and 13.9% abandons. R1 combines several measures: overtime for 2 payments agents (13:15–14:15), shifting both break blocks by 45 min, callbacks on both queues and 20% chat deflection. This gives 55.1% overall (payments 44.8%, general 68.2%), 13.0% abandons and 82.0% for the rest of the day. Escalation is required because 55% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). Only fixing the CRM issue, or decisions above supervisor level, can close the rest of the gap.","trade_offs":["P3 costs ₹540, ₹84 less than R1, and gives slightly better payments (45.6% vs 44.8%) and abandons (12.5% vs 13.0%). Overall it is lower (54.0% vs 55.1%) and general gets much less help (64.1% vs 68.2%).","P1 costs nothing but barely moves the window (50.0%). It also lowers the rest-of-day figure to 79.2%, against 81.0% with no action.","P2 (₹264) reaches only 50.9%, so it does not justify its cost compared with R1.","R2 would reach 57.2% at the same ₹624 but breaks CX-01: the known-issue message would target refund_status on payments, which is not rising. It is excluded."],"watch":"Watch payments service level and abandons from 12:45. Payments stays weakest even under R1 (44.8%). Check whether the 2 overtime agents actually accept, and track the CRM incident; if it is resolved early, handle times should fall and some actions can be stood down. Make sure the break shifts do not push rest-of-day service below about 80%."}
